explanation:
## What is a VAT (IVA) refund on debit purchases?

When you buy at a store in Argentina the price already includes **IVA (VAT)** — the standard rate is **21%**, with a reduced **10.5%** on some essentials. A reintegro (refund) returns a slice of that tax when you pay as an end consumer with a **debit card**. The benefit can come from a national scheme, a provincial program, or a promotion run by your own bank — and several of them can stack.

## How the calculation works

The VAT is embedded in the sticker price, so to isolate it you divide out the rate, then apply the refund percentage:

```
VAT contained = total ÷ (1 + VAT rate)  × VAT rate
Refund        = VAT contained × refund percentage
Net paid      = total − refund
```

On a $100,000 purchase at 21% IVA, the embedded tax is $100,000 ÷ 1.21 × 0.21 ≈ **$17,355**. A 10% reintegro returns about **$1,735**, so you effectively pay $98,265. The refund is a percentage *of the VAT*, not of the whole ticket — that is why the credit on your statement looks small relative to the spend.

## Refund rates by program and item

| Context | Typical refund | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Standard goods (21% IVA) | up to 21% of VAT | Full rate items: appliances, clothing, fuel |
| Essentials (10.5% IVA) | up to 10.5% of VAT | Reduced-rate basics: bread, milk, meat, produce |
| AUH / pension recipients | higher tier + monthly cap | Historically the most generous reintegro tier |
| Bank debit promo | 5%–20% off purchase | Bank-funded, separate from the tax refund |

*Rates and caps change with the regime in force; confirm the current scheme with ARCA (ex-AFIP) and your bank.*

## What lowers your real refund

- **Monthly caps.** Most programs refund only up to a ceiling per card per month (often a few tens of thousands of pesos). Spend above the cap gets no reintegro.
- **Card type.** The benefit is tied to **debit**; paying with credit usually forfeits the tax refund (though the card may offer its own cashback).
- **Eligible merchants.** Supermarkets, pharmacies and fuel stations commonly qualify; not every category does.
- **Reduced-rate items.** A 10.5% IVA product simply contains less tax to refund than a 21% one.

## Refund vs. cashback — not the same thing

A **VAT reintegro** gives back part of a tax you already paid to the state; a **cashback** is a marketing reward funded by the bank or card network. They are independent, can apply to the same purchase, and are calculated on different bases (tax vs. ticket total).

## Important note

This is an estimate. Actual reintegros depend on the scheme in force, your bank's terms, the IVA rate of each item, and the monthly cap. For the exact rules consult **ARCA (ex-AFIP)** and your card issuer.

faq.q: How does debit card VAT refund work?
faq.a: Many banks reimburse a percentage of VAT on purchases made with their debit cards.

faq.q: Is there a monthly cap on refunds?
faq.a: Yes, it depends on your bank (typically $5,000–$30,000 per month).
Grocery stores, pharmacies, and gas stations typically offer refunds.

faq.q: Can I combine multiple refund programs?
faq.a: Yes, provincial programs and bank reimbursements can stack on top of each other.
Generally not, but verify if your refund exceeds certain thresholds.

faq.q: When do refunds appear in my account?
faq.a: Usually at the close of your monthly statement, posted as a separate 'reintegro IVA' credit line rather than reducing each purchase at the till.

faq.q: Is a debit card refund program worth it?
faq.a: Yes, especially for recurring expenses and regular purchases.

faq.q: How does this compare to cashback credit cards?
faq.a: Similar concept—both provide purchasing incentives, but terms vary by issuer.
